title: Semiabelian geometric fibres of a commutative group scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G$ be a commutative group scheme over $S$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. For every algebraically closed field $k$ and morphism $s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$, form the base change $G_s$ with its induced group law [def-pc-base-change]. We say $G$ has semiabelian geometric fibres if for every such $s$ there exist $r\in\mathbf N$, an abelian variety $A$ over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and homomorphisms $i:(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_s$, $q:G_s\to A$, where the split torus is as in [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], such that $i$ identifies the split torus with the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$ and $q$ is locally surjective for the big fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]. Equivalently the resulting sequence $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_s\to A\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves. Rank zero is permitted. Over algebraically closed $k$, the connected smooth group $A$ is geometrically connected.
